stem:
Triangles $PQR$ and $XYZ$ are right-angled at $Q$ and $Y$. Hypotenuse $PR=XZ$, and leg $PQ=XY$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The triangles are congruent even if one of them is not right-angled.
The same three matching pieces also guarantee congruence for two non-right triangles under SSA.
The triangles are congruent by RHS: right angle, hypotenuse, and one corresponding leg.
The triangles are congruent because the letters $P,Q,R$ and $X,Y,Z$ look alike.

teacher.key_rationale: RHS needs both triangles right-angled, with equal hypotenuse and one equal corresponding side. Dropping the right-angle condition, extending to non-right SSA, or matching letters alone all miss RHS.
